 --> Odisha schools closed in 15 districts amid cyclone Akvan threat; check district-wise list
 Odisha has closed schools and educational institutions across 15 districts on November 20 as Cyclone Akvan threatens the state with heavy rainfall and strong winds. 
 Sheetal Kumari 
 November 20, 2026 / 11:00 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Cyclone Akvan Tracker: Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata Odisha schools closed due to severe cyclone Akvan.
 Closures affect multiple districts from Nov 20 to 21.
 IMD warns of heavy rain and winds up to 110 kmph.

 Schools and other educational institutions across several districts of Odisha will remain closed on Friday, November 20, as severe cyclonic storm Akvan approaches the state's coastline. District administrations have announced precautionary holidays to protect students and staff from the expected heavy rainfall, strong winds and adverse weather conditions. The closures cover government and private schools, while orders in some districts also include colleges, universities, technical institutions and Anganwadi centres.
 The holiday schedule differs across districts, with some administrations ordering closures only on November 20, while others have extended the shutdown until November 21. The state government had earlier directed educational institutions in six districts to remain closed from November 19 to 21. District Collectors have also been authorised to assess the weather situation and take further decisions depending on local conditions.
 According to district-wise announcements, educational institutions in Khordha, Cuttack, Rayagada, Koraput, Balasore, Malkangiri, Bhadrak, Ganjam, Gajapati, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Kandhamal, Subarnapur and Jajpur are among those affected by the precautionary closures.
 Odisha School Holiday Today: District-Wise List of School Closures
 The district administrations have announced different closure periods depending on the expected impact of the cyclone. While several districts have ordered schools to remain shut until November 20, institutions in six districts will continue to remain closed on November 21.

 Closure period Districts 
 Closed until November 20 Khordha, Cuttack, Rayagada, Koraput, Balasore, Malkangiri and Bhadrak 
 Closed until November 21 Ganjam, Gajapati, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri and Kandhamal 
 One-day closure on November 20 Subarnapur and Jajpur 
 In Subarnapur, the administration has ordered government, government-aided and private schools to remain closed on November 20. The directive also covers Kendriya Vidyalayas, Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas and Odisha Adarsha Vidyalayas. Anganwadi centres in the district will also remain shut.
 The Jajpur administration has separately declared a one-day holiday for government, government-aided and private schools on Friday.
 Cuttack has issued a wider closure order covering government, private and government-aided schools, colleges, universities, Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and polytechnics. Anganwadi centres have also been included in the directive. The decision follows the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall and high-velocity winds.
 Odisha Schools Closed Till November 21 in Six Districts
 The Odisha government had previously announced the closure of schools and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal from November 19 to 21.
 The Office of the Special Relief Commissioner has authorised the respective district Collectors to review local weather conditions and decide whether the holidays need to be extended. Collectors in other districts have also been instructed to monitor the situation and take precautionary measures wherever necessary.
 Parents, students and school authorities should follow the latest announcements issued by their respective district administrations, as closure orders may be revised depending on the cyclone's movement and intensity.
 Cyclone Akvan: IMD Issues Warning for Odisha Coast
 According to the IMD's November 19 bulletin, severe cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to move north-northwestwards and cross the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon on November 20.
 The weather system is likely to produce maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, with gusts reaching 110 kmph. The meteorological department has issued a cyclone warning for the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts.
 With the cyclone expected to affect coastal areas through heavy rainfall and powerful winds, district authorities have taken precautionary steps to minimise risks. Residents have been advised to follow official weather updates, adhere to government advisories and avoid unnecessary travel during adverse weather conditions.
 The administration's priority remains the safety of residents, particularly students and children attending educational institutions, as the storm approaches the Odisha coast.
